translation_notes: the single graph.add((s, p, o)) becomes a one-line island: RDFS.seeAlso -> rdfs:seeAlso, the subject and the loop variable stay interpolations ({self.identifier}, {s}). One of the three terms is absorbed by the notation, which is all this region offers.

the mechanical draft inserted the @prefix statements INSIDE the parenthesised `from rdflib import (...)` list, which is a syntax error; they were moved after the import. It also declared rdf:, unused here, which was dropped.
the loop stays a Python loop: ldpy has no island form for 'one statement per element of a list', so the island is evaluated once per iteration

self.graph is a plain attribute of infixowl's Individual (not a property), so the idiomatic `self.graph += g{...}` is available -- unlike the nanopub examples, where the target graphs are read-only properties. Graph.__iadd__ returns self, so the attribute is rebound to the same object and nothing observable changes.
RDFS becomes a dead name in the rdflib import line on the ldpy side; the line is left untouched (the extract carries the enclosing module's shared preamble, most of which is already unused here)

driver: the region is a property setter body, so a stand-in `self` supplies graph + identifier and is compared by graph isomorphism. Five fixtures: two URIRefs, a mix of URIRef/Literal/BNode objects, a blank-node subject, an empty list and None (the two early-return branches).
